title: The YM3812 OPL2 registers
covers: the registers of the YM3812 (OPL2) FM synthesizer as Yamaha's application manual describes them, and what MAME and DOSBox-X do for each

rows.text: Address $01 is used only by Yamaha for testing the LSI, and its bits are normally all 0.
A write to $01 with D5 set to 1 controls the output waveform.

closed.reason: marks every channel for re-preparation; no register behaviour

rows.text: Timer 1 is an 8-bit presettable counter, preset by the value written to address $02.
When timer 1 overflows, its flag is set and the preset value is loaded again.
In composite speech synthesis mode a timer 1 overflow sets all slots to Key-ON.
In that mode the slots then go immediately to Key-OFF.
Timer 1 overflows after (256-N1)*0.08 ms at 3.6 MHz; the multiplication sign and the sum for N1 are garbled in the capture.
The timer's overflow branch sets the overflow flag and the next trigger time and does no key-on.
The timer's overflow branch sets the overflow flag and the next trigger time and does no key-off.
MAME's operator reset sets the envelope attenuation to 0x3ff and the envelope state to release.
When an operator starts its attack with a cached attack rate of 62 or more, MAME sets its attenuation to 0 at once.
On an envelope tick MAME moves an operator from attack to decay at attenuation 0, and from decay to sustain once attenuation reaches the cached sustain level.
Outside attack MAME adds the rate's increment to the attenuation, clamped at 0x3ff; in attack, at a rate below 62, it adds (~attenuation*increment)>>4.
MAME's start of an attack puts the operator in the attack state, and does nothing when it is already in attack.
MAME's start of a release puts the operator in the release state, and does nothing when it is already in release.

rows.text: Timer 2 is an 8-bit presettable counter like timer 1, and $03 is its register.
Timer 1 has a resolution of 80 and timer 2 of 320; the unit is garbled in the capture.
Timer 2 overflows after (256-N2)*0.32 ms at 3.6 MHz; the multiplication sign and the sum for N2 are garbled in the capture.

rows.text: There are two timers, with resolutions of 80 and 320 (unit garbled in the capture), which can be started, stopped and flag-controlled.
This register starts, stops and flag-controls timers 1 and 2 through the bits D0, D1, D5, D6 and D7; some labels are garbled in the capture.
ST1: with 1 the preset is loaded into timer 1 and counting starts; with 0 timer 1 does not operate.
ST2 does the same for timer 2.
MASK T2: with 1 the flag of timer 2 is masked (always 0) and does not affect how timer 2 operates; the capture reads this bit as Ds.
MASK T1: masks the flag of timer 1; the capture reads this bit as De.
IRQ RESET: with 1 the flags of timers 1 and 2 are reset and the data of D0 to D5 is ignored.
After a write with D7 set, bit D7 is automatically reset to 0.
A write with bit 7 set stores that bit as 1 on top of the old bits.
The case body acts on the bits and stores no register data, so no D7 is kept to be reset.
MAME sets the status IRQ bit when a timer flag not hidden by the IRQ mask or the status mask is set, and clears the bit otherwise.

rows.text: The register selects music or speech synthesis mode and the keyboard split for rate key scaling.
CSM (D7) set to 1 selects the composite sine wave speech synthesis mode.
All channels must be in the Key-OFF state when CSM mode is selected.
NOTE SEL: with 0 the keyboard split is the second bit from the F-Number MSB, with 1 it is the MSB; the capture reads the bit label as De.
With NOTE SEL 0 the key code takes F-Number bit 9, the MSB, and with 1 bit 8, a comment says it is reversed from the manual.
With NOTE SEL 0 the key code takes F-Number bit 9, the MSB, and with 1 bit 8.
The branch for $08 only stores the value in reg08 and starts no speech synthesis.

rows.text: This register controls the multiple that converts the frequency data given by the envelope shape and F-Number into carrier and modulating wave frequencies.
MULTIPLE (D0 to D3) holds the multiple of the carrier or modulating wave frequency, as Table 3-1 lists; the capture reads the range as Do~Ds3.
KSR gives the key scaling of the rate; the capture reads the bit as Ds.
Key scaling of the rate simulates that natural instruments attack and decay faster at higher pitch, adding an offset to each rate (Table 3-2).
RATE = 4*R + Rks, R being the rate set and Rks the key scaling offset; RATE is 0 when R is 0; the product sign is garbled.
EG-TYP selects a diminishing sound with 0 and a connecting sound with 1, which differ in the use of the release rate; the capture reads the bit as Ds.
VIB is the vibrato on/off switch of the slot; the capture reads the bit as De.
Vibrato runs at 6.4 Hz with a 3.6 MHz master clock and its depth is set by VIB-DEPTH of the $BD register.
AM is the amplitude modulation on/off switch of the slot.
Amplitude modulation runs at 3.7 Hz with a 3.6 MHz master clock and its depth is set by AM-DEPTH of the $BD register.

rows.text: The total level controls the modulation factor and volume of the envelope generator output; KSL, like rate key scaling, makes the level fall as the interval rises.
Bits D0 to D5 hold the total level, which attenuates 0.75 dB per step, up to 47.25 dB; the capture reads the range as Do~Ds.
KSL (D6 and D7) controls level key scaling, which attenuates the level as the interval increases; the capture reads D6 as De.
The level key scaling attenuation can be set to none, 1.5 dB, 3 dB or 6 dB per octave.

rows.text: The attack rate sets the rising time of the sound and the decay rate the diminishing time after the attack; Table 3-6 gives the times.
The register holds the attack rate AR and the decay rate DR.
The envelope does not change when the rate is 0.

rows.text: For continuing sounds the sustain level is where the decaying sound becomes constant; for diminishing sounds it is where decay changes to release.
For continuing sounds the release rate is how fast the sound dies after Key-OFF; for diminishing sounds it governs the attenuation after the sustain level.
The register holds the sustain level SL in D4 to D7, where all four bits set mean 93 dB, and the release rate; the capture reads D4 as Da.
The attenuation time of the release rate is the same as that of the decay rate table.

rows.text: The registers give the interval and scale data; the F-Number is determined by both the $A* and the $B* registers.
The F-Number is ten bits: the eight bits of the $A* register and the lower two bits of the $B* register.
The F-Number gives the scale and is determined by the procedure outlined below the entry.

rows.text: The required frequency is obtained by giving its phase increment, which is determined by the F-Number, Block and Multiple.
BLOCK, in bits D2 to D4, gives the octave information; the capture reads D4 as Da4.
Key-ON: with 1 the channel is on and voiced, with 0 it is in Key-OFF; the capture reads the bit as Ds.
The phase increment is AP = fmus*2^19/fsam with fsam = fM/72, 50 kHz at 3.6 MHz; the capture garbles some symbols.
The increment is kept for one octave and shifted per octave, as AP = 2^B*F'*MUL; the capture garbles the F-Number and Block formulas.

rows.text: The register controls AM and vibrato depth, the selection of rhythm mode and the ON/OFF of the rhythm instruments.
D5 (RHYTHM) set to 1 selects the rhythm sound mode; the capture reads the bit as Ds.
In rhythm mode channels 7 to 9 are used for rhythm sounds, so melody sounds are limited to six.
Bits D0 to D4 switch the individual rhythm instruments on and off; the capture reads the range as Do~Ds.
The key-on registers $B6, $B7 and $B8 must always be 0 (the capture shows 9) and slot data must suit each rhythm sound.
D6 (VIB-DEPTH) is the vibrato depth bit: 14 cent when 1 and 7 cent when 0; the capture reads the bit as De.
D7 (AM-DEPTH) is the AM depth bit: 4.8 dB when 1; the value for 0 is garbled in the capture.
Turning rhythm mode off restores the melody synth of channel 6 and sets key-off on every rhythm operator.

rows.text: The register determines the modulation factor of self-feedback and the type of FM modulation.
CONNECTION: 0 selects FM modulation of the two slots, 1 connects them in parallel for sine wave output in the composite mode.
FEEDBACK holds the modulation factor of feedback FM modulation of the first slot; the capture reads the range as Di~Ds3.

rows.text: With bit D5 of $01 at 0 the OPL2 is fully compatible with the YM3526 and a sine input stays a sine (bit and address garbled in the capture).
With bit D5 of $01 at 1 the input sine wave comes out as the distorted waves of Table 3-10; the capture garbles the bit and address.
The registers $E0 to $F5 hold the wave select (Table 3-10).
DOSBox-X picks an operator's wave by indexing a table of eight waveform handlers, WaveForm0 to WaveForm7, with the masked wave select value.
